A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 19-page versions of AnomalyVFM, including Supplementary Material Sections A-G. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot and few-shot anomaly-detection experiments, ablations, runtime measurements and additional empirical analyses in the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Sections 5-6 and the supplement, including benchmark comparisons, ablations and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 retain the same three-stage data generator, LoRA adaptation, decoder, losses and inference procedure. Correcting 'aLoRA' to 'a LoRA' is a spacing edit, not a different component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine industrial and nine medical datasets, plus few-shot detection on MVTec AD and VisA. Synthetic training-data coverage and the generation lists in Appendix G are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in main Tables 2-4 and 6 and supplementary Table 1. The newly cited ObjectCore work appears only in related work, not as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain the same auxiliary-data conventions, AUROC/F1-max metrics, preprocessing, training budgets and evaluation procedures. This includes 500 training iterations with batch size 32 and the same 1-, 2- and 4-shot comparisons.

E4.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain identical analyses of generator choice, filtering, foreground selection, confidence loss, adapter design, model size and dataset scale. Generation failure cases and qualitative segmentation examples also match.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and plots without error bars remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Benchmark, ablation, runtime and supplementary results are unchanged, including plotted trends and qualitative examples. For example, Table 2 retains AnomalyVFM's 94.1% image-level and 96.9% pixel-level AUROC, versus Bayes-PFL's 90.8% and 96.0%.

T1.justification: The generation equations, sampling definitions and loss formulations in Equations 1-4 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: synthetic data generation and parameter-efficient VFM adaptation for zero-shot detection, with medical generalisation and few-shot applicability. The claimed 3.3-percentage-point industrial image-level AUROC advantage is unchanged.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability claims remain unchanged. Section 6 and Appendix A-B retain the same limitations concerning generation time, unrealistic medical images, imperfect filtering and opportunities to improve dataset diversity.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware and timing disclosures, generation prompts, filtering threshold, dataset statistics and Appendix G tag lists are identical. The project-page link also remains the same.

R1.justification: v2 adds ObjectCore as reference 20 and cites it among embedding-based anomaly-detection methods in Section 2. This modestly expands related-work coverage without changing the paper's novelty positioning; other citation-number shifts reflect renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 lightly edits related-work prose, corrects 'gemeralise' and 'aLoRA', adds the codeplain affiliation and updates author markers. It also completes SALAD's bibliographic page range. Section order and the substantive narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation block shifts first-page content, and text and references reflow locally. Printed page numbers are removed throughout. Figures and tables retain their content and design, with no added or removed displays.

improvement.justification: The ObjectCore citation and light copyediting provide slight editorial polish, while the method, evidence, reproducibility information and appendix remain unchanged. These limited benefits, alongside removal of printed page numbers, do not produce a meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
